purpose: Static input for the automated A/B, pool-expansion, rebuild and reporting regression tests. It stands in for the gitignored maintainer artifact data/05_evaluation/retrieval_results.json so those tests run on a fresh clone. It is never produced by the code under test.
kind: frozen retrieval-only baseline (60 cases, 10-document release corpus)
generated_by: evaluate-retrieval against a live OpenAI-embedded index (text-embedding-3-small)
content_sha256_basis: SHA-256 of the file with line endings normalised to LF (a Windows checkout may hold CRLF)
derivation: Byte-for-byte copy of the source artifact except CRLF line endings were normalised to LF. No field was edited, removed or re-serialised, so the recorded evaluation_result_id still reproduces from the content.
sanitization: Scanned before freezing: no absolute paths, user names, API keys or environment values. Retrieved chunk text is not stored, only chunk ids, document ids, repository-relative source paths, headings and similarity values. tests/unit/test_frozen_baseline_fixture.py enforces this on every run.
why_the_complete_run_is_kept: The regression tests assert behaviour over all 60 cases (one retrieval per case, case_count == 60, baseline identity per case, the evaluation_result_id and aggregate metrics of the baseline arm). A subset would change what they prove.
cross_checks: evaluation_result_id, per-case metrics and aggregate metrics recompute from the stored chunks with the project's own functions
queries, expected risk and expected documents equal tests/01_test_questions.md and tests/02_expected_answers.md
maintainer_artifact: data/05_evaluation/retrieval_results.json may still exist locally. When it does, tests/unit/test_frozen_baseline_fixture.py (local_artifact) requires it to equal this fixture and fails if it has diverged; when it is absent that single test skips.
regeneration: Only when the frozen baseline is deliberately replaced: copy the new retrieval_results.json over the fixture (LF endings), update content_sha256, evaluation_result_id, index_fingerprint and source_* here, and review the A/B artifacts that cite the old id.
